title: The Telegram bot token is written to the logs on every failed alert: the token is part of the request URL, the axios error is logged whole as err, and its config.url carries the URL (reproduced offline); a token symbol that breaks the Markdown is enough to cause a failure

evidence.note: axios.post(TELEGRAM_API, ...) and on any error log.warn({ err: error }, 'Telegram alert error')
no redact configuration; pino serializes err with its enumerable properties

evidence.ref: node tg-log-repro.js (scratch folder outside the repo (Node 22.16.0; no src/ import, no .env, no live DB; loopback 127.0.0.1 only); axios 1.10.0 CJS build and pino 10.3.1 from the repo node_modules with the logger.ts options; fake sentinel token; POST to 127.0.0.1:1)
evidence.note: output: token present in log line: true; the line carries "url":"http://127.0.0.1:1/bot<fake token>/sendMessage" inside err.config

sibling_sites_checked: Both Telegram send sites in the slice (notifier.ts:44 and :80) use the same URL and the same err logging. Ways a send fails: network errors, Telegram 429, and HTTP 400 when parse_mode Markdown meets an unbalanced * or _ (the deployer-chosen token symbol goes in unescaped, AUD-BUY-022). Where logs go: stdout, persisted when the operator redirects it (the data/*capture*.log files; AUD-TX-014 records that the backup copies passed the D-22 exact-value check, which includes TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN). No axios timeout is set (AUD-EXIT-021).
severity_rationale: S2 EXPOSURE, the same class and grade as AUD-TX-014: a credential crosses into the logs under ordinary failures, and an outsider can trigger the failure through a token name. The bot token lets whoever reads the logs send messages as the bot and read the bot chat; it does not move funds.
recommendation: Log only error.message / code / response status for Telegram failures and add logger-level redaction (card TX-04); check persisted logs and rotate the bot token if any contains it.
